units.source_text: 这样的信辅，所有的事情都是从书里学来的。

en.t: This was the kind of man Shinsuke was: he had learned everything from books.

units.source_text: 至少可以说，我没有任何一件事不是从书本里得到启发的。

en.t: At the very least, one could say that there was not a single thing in me that had not been inspired by books.

units.source_text: 事实上，他是一个为了思考人生而无视街头行人的人。

en.t: In fact, he was the sort of person who ignored passersby on the street in order to think about life.

units.source_text: 或者说，与观察行人相比，他更愿意思考书本里的人生。

en.t: Or rather, instead of observing passersby, he preferred to think about the lives found in books.

units.source_text: 或者可以说这是他理解人生的曲线手段吧！

en.t: Perhaps one could say that this was his indirect way of understanding life.

units.source_text: 可是，对于他来说，街头行人不过是普通行人罢了。

en.t: But to him, the passersby on the street were nothing more than ordinary passersby.

units.source_text: 他为了理解他们的人生——理解他们的爱，理解他们的憎恨，理解他们的虚荣心，唯有读书一个方法。

en.t: To understand their lives, to understand their love, their hatred, and their vanity, he had only one method: reading books.

units.source_text: 书籍，尤其是世纪末欧洲出版的小说和戏剧，终于在他冷峻的心里，开启了一幕幕人间喜剧。

en.t: Books, especially the novels and plays published in fin de siecle Europe, at last opened scene after scene of human comedy in his austere heart.

units.source_text: 不，毋宁说是让他看到了自己不分善恶的灵魂，不仅限于他自己的人生，他也因此看到了本所街町的自然之美。

en.t: No, it would be better to say that they showed him his own soul, undivided by good and evil; and beyond his own life, they also let him see the natural beauty of the streets of Honjo.

units.source_text: 但是，让他观看自然的眼睛更加锐利的依然是靠几本喜欢的书的启发——尤其是元禄时代的绯谐。

en.t: Yet what made his eyes sharper in looking at nature was still the inspiration of a few beloved books, especially the haikai of the Genroku era.

units.source_text: 正是因为他读了那些绯句，诸如，“近京城观山形”、“郁金田秋高气爽”、“黑夜飞过苍鹭啼”等，他才发现本所街町前所未有的自然之美。

en.t: It was precisely because he had read such haiku as "near the capital, seeing the shape of the mountains," "in the turmeric fields, the autumn sky is clear," and "a heron cries as it flies through the dark night" that he discovered an unprecedented natural beauty in the streets of Honjo.

units.source_text: 这种从“书籍到现实”的过程，对信辅来说就是真理。

en.t: For Shinsuke, this process of moving from books to reality was truth itself.

units.source_text: 他在自己的半生中也曾对几个女子有过爱慕之情。

en.t: In the first half of his life, he too had felt affection for several women.

units.source_text: 但这并没让他了解到书本之外的女性之美。

en.t: But this did not teach him the beauty of women outside of books.

units.source_text: 从戈蒂耶、巴尔扎克、托尔斯坦的梳理，信辅才了解到女性“穿透阳光的耳朵”和“落在脸颊上的睫毛的剪影”的美好。

en.t: Only through the ordering of Gautier, Balzac, and Tolstoy did Shinsuke come to know the beauty of a woman's "ears translucent in the sunlight" and "the shadow of eyelashes falling on her cheeks."

units.source_text: 时至今日，信辅欣赏的女性之美还是这些。

en.t: Even now, these are still the kinds of feminine beauty that Shinsuke admires.

units.source_text: 如果不是从书本里学到了这些的话，可能他只能知道女性就是雌性吧。

en.t: If he had not learned these things from books, perhaps he would only have known that women were female.
